items.question: What attainment makes a practitioner dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation constitute a great accomplishment.
Such accomplishment can arise for a practitioner.
Being dear to the yoginīs is linked to this attainment.
items.inference: One who attains the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: He may become dear to the yoginīs through the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: Which chapter emerges in the context of Candra-dvīpa?
premises: A chapter is identified by ordinal number.
This chapter is said to have emerged in Candra-dvīpa.
The ordinal given is ninth.
items.inference: The ninth chapter is the one that emerged in Candra-dvīpa.
items.plain_english: The ninth chapter, emerged in Candra-dvīpa.

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self in this practice?
premises: The self is described as surrounded by fire.
The self is described as standing on one foot.
These attributes define a specific contemplative posture.
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self surrounded by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: Visualize oneself surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What has been revealed to the speaker by the deity today?
premises: The speaker addresses the deity directly.
The determination of knowledge is the subject revealed.
This revelation has occurred today.
items.inference: The determination of knowledge has been made manifest to the speaker today.
items.plain_english: O God, today the determination of knowledge has been made manifest to me.

items.question: What division does the speaker seek to know fully and endlessly?
premises: The object of inquiry is a division.
This division consists of eight octads.
The speaker seeks to know it fully and endlessly.
items.inference: The speaker seeks to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.
items.plain_english: And to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.

items.question: How is the wheel quickly accomplished in the secret place?
premises: A secret place is invoked as the locus.
The wheel is the object of accomplishment.
The accomplishment occurs quickly.
items.inference: In the secret place, O Bhairava, the wheel is quickly accomplished.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic role of yathā is slightly ambiguous without broader context.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell how the wheel is quickly accomplished in the secret place.

items.question: Why does Bhairava praise the Great Goddess for her question?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval.
He states he has been asked something.
What was asked is hard to obtain even by the gods.
items.inference: Bhairava praises the Great Goddess because she has asked about something rare even for the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O Great Goddess! I have been asked about something hard to obtain even by the gods.

items.question: Where are the syllables kṣa and laṃ located in the subtle body?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra.
The syllable laṃ is associated with the forehead.
These are specific placements in the body.
items.inference: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form; translated as forehead region.
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Where are the syllables ṣa and śa placed in the body?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region.
The syllable śa is placed in the heart.
These placements are stated in sequence.
items.inference: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region and the syllable śa is in the heart.
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

items.question: What does the deity instruct the beloved to hear after declaring the place-wheels?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared.
Their meditation remains to be explained.
The beloved is commanded to listen.
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the deity instructs the beloved to hear their meditation.
items.plain_english: The place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first octad described?
premises: The lotus is described as divine.
It has eight spokes or petals.
It is adorned by the first octad.
items.inference: The divine lotus is eight-spoked and adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: A divine eight-spoked lotus, adorned by the first octad.

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner with equanimous mind abandon through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an equanimous mind.
Village dharma is identified as something to abandon.
The abandonment is prescribed for such a practitioner.
items.inference: Through practice, one with an equanimous mind should abandon village dharma.
uncertainties: grāma dharmañ may refer to conventional social duties; exact nuance context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Through practice, with an equanimous mind, one should abandon the dharma of the village.

items.question: What powers arise from this practice according to the teaching?
premises: Knowledge of distant hearing is mentioned.
Paralysis of bonds is mentioned.
These are presented as attained results.
items.inference: The practice yields knowledge of distant hearing and the paralysis of bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa stobham could also imply arresting or stopping bonds; translated as paralysis.
items.plain_english: Knowledge of hearing from afar, and likewise the paralysis of bonds, O beloved.

items.question: What further attainments are briefly stated for the practitioner?
premises: Immortality is named as an attainment.
Transformation is named as an attainment.
These are stated in brief.
items.inference: In brief, the practitioner attains immortality and transformation.
items.plain_english: Likewise, O Goddess, in brief, immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled lotus characterized in meditation?
premises: A second eight-petaled lotus is described.
It is associated with meditation on fire or radiance.
It is well illuminated.
items.inference: The second eight-petaled lotus is well illuminated by meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled lotus, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes one-pointed in meditation.
Such a practitioner acts upon form.
The action produces forms in many ways.
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can create forms in many ways.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume forms in many ways.

items.question: What destructive power can the practitioner wield when angered?
premises: The practitioner is described as angry.
The object of destruction is the entire triple world.
The triple world includes moving and unmoving beings.
items.inference: When angry, the practitioner can destroy the entire triple world with all its moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What is the liberating function of the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is identified.
It is characterized as a liberator.
Its scope is the nine principles.
items.inference: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.
items.plain_english: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from this wheel's practice?
premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is mentioned.
Seeing from very far away is mentioned.
Both are presented as attained results.
items.inference: The practice brings destruction of wrinkles and grey hair and the ability to see from very far away.
items.plain_english: The destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.question: How should a dedicated practitioner cultivate multiple forms in solitude?
premises: The practice is to be done in solitude.
The practitioner should be intent on meditation.
The practitioner is instructed to make forms in many ways.
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, the practitioner should create forms in many ways.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create forms in many ways.

items.question: What result comes to one devoted to constant practice?
premises: The practitioner is devoted to constant practice.
Immortality is named as the result.
The statement is emphatic.
items.inference: One devoted to constant practice indeed attains immortality.
items.plain_english: One intent on constant practice indeed attains immortality.

items.question: How does non-eating by day affect age and death?
premises: Non-eating by day is specified as a practice.
Age and death are the targets affected.
A future outcome is stated.
items.inference: Through non-eating by day, one will overcome death associated with age.
uncertainties: The exact sense of vayo mṛtyuṃ gamiṣyate is compressed; interpreted as overcoming age-related death.
items.plain_english: Indeed, by not eating during the day, one will overcome death due to age.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant yogic practice over time?
premises: Constant practice through yoga is the means.
A specific age-form is indicated as sixteen years.
This form becomes attainable.
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.
uncertainties: dvi aṣṭa varṣa ākṛtiḥ interpreted as the form of sixteen years.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power arises from always contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: A smoke-colored object is to be contemplated always.
The triple world is named as the object affected.
The practitioner gains the power to shake it.
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world.
items.plain_english: Always contemplating a smoke-colored form, O beloved, one may shake the triple world.
